title: Four Null Spacetime Theory VI: Quantum Geometry of Four Null Cells: the Quantum Cell, the Counting Action, Hinge Characters, Horizons and the Quantum Program
content: This is the sixth and final paper of a series on Four Null Spacetime Theory, in which spacetime is built from finite cells spanned by four lightlike vectors in perfect balance. The first five papers established the classical theory: the cell, its gluing, its propagation and interaction, its fields and its characteristic dynamics. This paper asks what a quantum theory of the cells must be, collects the quantum ingredients the program already supplies, and reports what can be established about them now. The relational clock selects SU(2) as the group of a quantum cell, and a quantized generator is null as an operator. Four spin one half legs give a two dimensional cell whose mean geometry is exactly the balanced cell; it carries the E representation of the generator permutations, its chiral states are the eigenstates of oriented volume, and a reflection exchanges them, which suggests, as a hypothesis, that the discrete reflection of classical gluing is the quantum orientation of the cell. Each individual pair product, and every operator symmetric under all permutations of the legs, is blind to that orientation, but the commutator of two pair products is the oriented volume and distinguishes it. The counting action of Paper II is blind to how curvature is distributed and periodic in its coupling, so a measure must select geometry, and in the route of exact balance the classical limit must emerge by coarse graining. The hinge characters take exact values that act as curvature selection rules. Local moves preserving balance exist; in short Monte Carlo runs the curvature per cell rises without weights and follows the sign of the action weight, a trend rather than an established phase. Horizons count cells of one universal area, so one bit per crossing cell would give a cell length of 1.10 Planck lengths, but a fabric cut sharply along a null surface exposes one to four faces per cell, and the entropy per area of the actual glued state remains to be derived. No result here establishes a quantum theory of Four Null spacetime; the paper ends with the program, its decisive Monte Carlo test and the criteria that would falsify it, and with the state of the series as a whole.
